purpose: Follow the production, maturation and transport sites.
writtenEquivalent: Sperm form in seminiferous tubules, mature in the epididymis and move through the vas deferens, ejaculatory duct and urethra. Accessory glands add fluid to semen.

purpose: Distinguish the reproductive-cell stages from their supporting cells.
writtenEquivalent: A primary spermatocyte completes two meiotic divisions to produce four haploid spermatids. These differentiate into sperm. Sertoli cells provide support; interstitial cells release testosterone.

purpose: Identify where sperm develop and where maturation continues.
writtenEquivalent: Developing cells are found within seminiferous tubules. Their later stages approach the lumen. Sperm then enter the epididymis, where maturation develops the capacity for movement.

purpose: Locate the ovary, oviduct, uterus, cervix and vagina.
writtenEquivalent: An oocyte is released from the ovary and guided toward the oviduct. Fertilization normally occurs in the oviduct. Implantation occurs later in the endometrium of the uterus.

purpose: Separate ovarian events from uterine events.
writtenEquivalent: Follicles develop and release estrogen before ovulation. After ovulation, the corpus luteum releases progesterone and some estrogen. Menstrual flow overlaps the early follicular phase of the next cycle.

purpose: Trace the estrogen rise, LH surge and later progesterone rise.
writtenEquivalent: Sustained high estrogen before ovulation promotes an LH surge. The surge helps trigger ovulation. The corpus luteum then releases progesterone; its later regression allows hormone support to fall.
